thread.title: Dow Jones Tries To End Bearish Action | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Tries To End Bearish Action | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average rallied more than 2.1% in early-afternoon trade Wednesday, trying to halt a massive four-session slide in which the blue-chip gauge plummeted 8%. But the Nasdaq composite is leading the rebound in stocks today , aided by institutional bargain-hunting in the FANG stocks .
Apple ( AAPL ), meanwhile, is also trying to stop a four-day selling skid with a gain of more than 3.7%. Volume is running at more than 40% its usual daily pace of 43.6 million shares per day. The iPhone giant is undergoing its steepest correction since marking a 45% drop from September 2012 to April 2013.
IBD actively covered Apple in the Stock Market Today column from October 2016 to January 2017 as the iPhone giant set up a first-stage base, then broke out of a perfect cup with handle and a 118.12 correct buy point on Jan. 6, 2017.
At 1 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq composite, which hit the technical definition of a bear market during last week's waterfall-style decline, rose more than 3.3%. If it holds that gain, it would the biggest single-session gain since a 3.3% rise on March 26 for the premier index of growth stocks.
Big Caps On Nasdaq Outperform The Dow Jones Industrials Too The Nasdaq 100-tracking Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) ETF rallied 3.6%, beating a 2.2% advance by the S&P 500. Volume is running lower vs. the same time on Tuesday, when Wall Street held a short trading session that ended at 1 p.m. ET.
Apparel, retail, software and fiber optic gear stocks paced the fairly broad rally as nearly three dozen of the IBD 197 industry groups jumped 1.5% or more. See the daily performance here or go to the Stock Lists section of Investors.com, then click on IBD Data Tables .
Department store, variety, apparel, internet and home furnishings retailers all gained 2% or more as groups. On MarketSmith , no stocks were posting breakouts from solid bases. However, MarketSmith notes that as many as 531 stocks were rising in above-average volume, vs. just 40 stocks falling in heavy trade. It's been the opposite trend (many more stocks falling in big turnover vs. up stocks in active trading) for most of the past eight weeks.
The Dow utility average lagged on Wednesday following Tuesday's Christmas holiday, falling around 0.1%. The Dow Jones transports rose 2.5%.
The Innovator IBD 50 ( FFTY ) gained more than 2.2% as it too seeks to lick its big wounds. The ETF has dropped nearly 35% from a 52-week peak of 38.79. The ETF focusing on high-growth companies gained 34% in 2017. SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) gained 0.6%, lagging the major indexes. But the gold-tracking fund is having an excellent quarter, up 7%.
The ETF is forming a saucer pattern .
Retail And Consumer Stocks Lead Rebound The day's top performer is the shoe making group, led by Dow Jones Industrial member Nike ( NKE ). The shoe and athletic apparel king rallied nearly 3% to 70.14.
While the stock trades 18% below its 52-week peak of 86.04, it's definitely suffered less damage than the major indexes. Hence, check out its rising relative strength line, drawn in blue in every IBD chart and in MarketSmith .
When a stock prepares a new base ahead of a potential breakout, watch its relative strength line. Often, the biggest stock market winners will show an RS line vaulting into new high ground on the breakout day or soon afterward.
Nike, for now, is still trying to bottom out. The big cap still trades well below its 50- and 200-day moving averages. IBD Stock Checkup notes that Nike scores a high Composite Rating of 93 on a scale of 1 to 99.
In Other Financial Markets Gold futures lost some of their early advance, while West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures jumped more than 7% to $45.76 a barrel. Earlier this week, crude oil hit as low as $42.36, the lowest since June 2017.
The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year bond rebounded 4 basis points to 2.78%. The yield had plunged 19 basis points since Dec. 3 as investors sold equities hard and moved into safe havens including Treasuries.
CME Group currently shows a small yet growing bet among bond futures traders that the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates in 2019.
The Fed Watch survey of fed funds futures activity now indicates a very slim 4.5% probability that the U.S. central bank will cut rates by a quarter point at the end of its September meeting in 2019. By December the same year, the probability of at least a 25-basis-point shave grows to 12%.
Earlier this month, the Federal Reserve hiked short-term interest rates by a quarter point for the fourth time this year and the ninth time since December 2015, setting a target rate of 2.25%-2.5% on overnight loans to Wall Street firms and other major banks.
